decisions.summary: env.py tolerates a database ahead on the opt-in chain - FINDING-3.3
decisions.rationale: Fixes a bug I introduced in DECISION-3.2. Hiding 0002 from the default version_locations stopped `alembic upgrade head` applying it, but also stopped the default config recognising a database that had legitimately applied it - so every ordinary deploy after the opt-in died with 'Can't locate revision identified by 0002'. I changed what the tool can see rather than what it does, and the consequence landed in the one place nobody tests: the second deploy.
decisions.tradeoff: env.py now knows migrations/deferred/ exists. Deliberately NOT a blanket ignore - a revision in neither chain still raises.
decisions.test_implication: Assert the tolerance boundary: an unknown revision in neither chain must still fail loudly. Also assert a FRESH database still gets all five tables - the probe originally shared Alembic's connection, leaving an open transaction that silently rolled the migration back while reporting success.

decisions.summary: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside an autocommit block - FINDING-3.4
decisions.rationale: Plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock blocking every INSERT/UPDATE for the whole build, on the two tables the pipeline writes to every tick and on a table that by definition holds thousands of rows by the time this is worth running. CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction because it must see other transactions commit between its two passes.
decisions.tradeoff: Those statements lose the migration's transaction: if the second index fails the first is already committed. Both use IF NOT EXISTS. A failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index that still slows writes and that IF NOT EXISTS considers present - the detection query is documented in the migration.
decisions.test_implication: Assert both CONCURRENTLY statements and the autocommit block; verify pg_index reports no invalid indexes after a real build.

decisions.summary: Digest URL validation is per quote, not per document - FINDING-3.5
decisions.rationale: _URL_RE.search(prose) asked whether the document contains a link anywhere, which one linked quote satisfied for all ten. The realistic failure is the model dropping some links, not all of them.
decisions.tradeoff: Needs a notion of what a quote is. Blocks (consecutive `>` lines plus the first non-blank line after) rather than lines, because a quote is routinely split across lines with the link last, or followed by an attribution line carrying the URL.
decisions.test_implication: Multi-line quotes with a trailing link, quote-then-blank-then-attribution, nested >>, prose with no quotes, and a ten-quote/nine-link digest that must name its offender.

test_targets: _quote_blocks directly: multi-line quotes with the link on the last line; quote, blank line, then attribution carrying the URL; nested >>; prose with no quotes at all
A digest with ten quotes and nine links is rejected and names the offender
env.py tolerance boundary: a revision in NEITHER chain must still fail loudly (stops DECISION-4.1 degenerating into 'ignore unknown revisions')
alembic upgrade head on a FRESH database still creates all five tables - regression hit during this build, where a shared probe connection rolled the migration back while reporting success
Concurrent index construction under concurrent writes if cheap to arrange; otherwise assert the autocommit block and IF NOT EXISTS textually
Re-running the opt-in config when both indexes already exist is a no-op (IF NOT EXISTS)
known_edge_cases: FULL SUITE: 102 passed, 0 failed, 0 SKIPPED. Integration tests ran on the Builder's machine for the first time, against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.13 + pgvector 0.8.5 cluster on port 55440 (the host's Homebrew cluster owns 5432 and holds four unrelated project databases; the integration conftest TRUNCATEs, so it could not be pointed there).

Migration lifecycle verified by hand against the database: default -> 0001/0 indexes; opt-in -> 0002/2 indexes, both vector_cosine_ops, zero invalid; default again -> rc 0, unchanged; opt-in downgrade -> 0001/0 indexes.
A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an invalid index that IF NOT EXISTS treats as present. Detection query is in the migration docstring.

findings.detail: A clean install pulls greenlet through sqlalchemy[asyncio], and its Alembic executable migrates a fresh database.
Default head is 0001 with zero HNSW indexes; the opt-in config sees 0002 and creates exactly two cosine indexes. TEST-CONFLICT-3.1 is resolved.
After the deferred command records 0002, the next normal alembic upgrade head exits 255 because the default configuration cannot locate revision 0002.
HNSW indexes use blocking CREATE INDEX inside a transaction even though the deployed PostgreSQL and pgvector support concurrent HNSW construction.
Aggregate URL validation accepts a digest with one linked quote and another unlinked quote, violating the per-quote requirement.
Blank, truncated, and fully linkless output is rejected before persistence or delivery; cluster IDs come from the ranking used for the prompt.
An accepted batch ID is logged at ERROR if tracking persistence fails, and the exception still propagates.
Reddit preserves partial progress across three failure domains; HN isolates unusable timestamps and attaches UTC to naive values.
DELETE-based reclustering is FK-safe on live PostgreSQL and preserves embeddings.
Compose services are healthy and loopback-bound; invalid log levels safely fall back to INFO.

findings.target: manual LLM and digest acceptance criteria
findings.detail: Pain-point normalization, vertical disagreements, and digest usefulness still require human review of actual model output.

open_blockers.detail: Manual LLM and digest quality criteria have no assertion form: pain-point normalization, vertical disagreements, and digest usefulness need a human reading real model output. Unchanged since cycle 1 and now the only open item in the protocol.
